families.title: PC cracktros and keygen intros
families.overview:
Checked against Pouet and Demozoo page by page (about 60 Pouet production pages read for credits and comments, their screenshots viewed as contact sheets, and about 45 Demozoo entries fetched as a second source), plus Wikipedia, Lode Vandevenne's effect tutorials and one blog write-up. Defacto2 is still unreachable (HTTP 403 to fetch, a bot-verification page in the browser, which I did not try to pass), and the web-search allowance for this session was already used up, so nothing here rests on search results.

The main finding stands: there is no single "Razor 1911 look" on PC. Going through Razor's Pouet list (305 entries, 189 of them DOS/Windows/Linux, not the "600+" the research claimed) the screenshots fall into these phases: (1) 1990-93 DOS loaders: a red capsule logo on blue gradient bars with a huge gradient scroller (Silent Shadow, with Skillion), a flaming, dripping logo over a starfield (1992 loader, Maelstrom 1993), a bronze extruded serif logo (Battle Chess 4000, 1993); (2) 1993-94 trainer menus; (3) the 1996-98 numbered DOS cracktros by Hetero of SAC, almost all PC conversions of Amiga intros: flat colour field, pixel logo, centred presents-text, one effect; (4) 1998-2000 Win9x screens with painted fantasy art and a fill-in template; (5) 2001-03 one-idea cracktros with Dubmood music; (6) the 2006 comeback cartoon and 2007 keygen templates with the same mascot; (7) 2010-12 rez-coded rainbow cube and glenz work; (8) the 2016 chrome-spheres cracktro by XT95; (9) 2024-26: text-mode installers drawn by Goto80, desktop-shattering "D-cracktros", the BIOS-screen dentro CMOS Cosmos (1st, Compusphere 2025) and the anniversary demo Razor1911 (1st, Revision 2026). The logo changes nearly every time; the rainbow block logo many people think of as "the" Razor logo is, according to Pouet comments by ACiD's radman and by rez, an ACiD text-art logo by JED from 1996.

Around Razor sit the broader schools: early-90s DOS VGA loaders (THG, INC, USA/Fairlight, TRSI), mid-90s Mode-X conversions of Amiga intros (SAC for Razor, Hybrid, Prestige), Win9x rip installers and trainers (Class, Myth, Hoodlum, Deviance), and the 2004-11 Win32 "new old-school" revival (Hoodlum, Deviance, Reloaded, Skid Row, Genesis with Titan/TRSI coders and artists).

I return 14 styles: the 13 submitted were kept in substance, with "Lit and liquid" merged into two neighbours, the recent Razor text-mode installers split out from the skinned installers because they can be done as pure text, and one new Razor style added (BIOS setup hijack). If a shorter list is wanted, the ones most distinct from the existing six and best sourced are: chrome spheres over checkerboard, neon cube field, text-mode poster installer, BIOS setup hijack, pencil on paper, fake desktop takeover, trainer menu and the Razor flat-field layout. Keygen windows by TSRh, AiR and CORE were named in the brief but could not be researched (no search budget, Defacto2 blocked); the existing keygen-dialog style covers that object, and the only keygen material confirmed here is Razor's 2007 templates (a dancing egg-headed mascot above a gold GENERATE KEY plate; graphics GB, code blkpanther, music Dubmood).

Motion is inferred from comments and effect names, not watched: every visual description comes from a single Pouet screenshot per production. SVG techniques marked "tested" were tested by the original researcher in Chromium only; I did not re-run them.

styles.name: Razor 1911 DOS cracktro: flat field, pixel logo, presents-text
styles.era: 1996-1998, MS-DOS (320x240x8 Mode-X, GUS/SoundBlaster per Demozoo); Razor 1911's numbered cracktro series made with Superior Art Creations, code by Hetero
styles.what_it_is: The small numbered intros that ran in front of Razor's mid-90s game releases: one flat colour field, a pixel logo across the top, a few centred lines of blocky text, one background effect and a looping tracker tune. Almost all are PC conversions of older Amiga intros (Pouet commenters name Paso for #7, Aspect for #01, Supplex for Arnie 3, Skid Row for #06, and Demozoo tags #10 melon-dezign-inspired), which is exactly why they feel 'Amiga' on a PC. The release titles shown in them are filler: Demozoo lists blank template versions.
visual_signature: One saturated flat background per intro: deep aubergine (#09), pale grey-green (#10), lilac (#7), navy (#5)

A different hand-pixelled logo each time, pinned to the top edge: tan bevelled italic capitals with pointed serifs (#09, logo by Poise per Demozoo), a multicolour script wordmark with a flower (#7, logo by Dream Design), a green outline logo on navy (#5)
A small wooden-looking plaque or bar directly under the logo carrying the release title (#09)
A centred column of wide, letterspaced capitals: group name between two hearts, stars or arrows, a dashed rule, a 'proudly presents on <date>' line, then the title between asterisks

Exactly one background effect: large pale cogs meshing slowly behind the text (#10), a lilac-and-white checker floor rotating in perspective with distance fog (#7), or nothing but a fading text writer (#5)
Text is white with a 1px dark outline so it reads over the effect; #5 sets red and magenta text and magenta dashed rules on navy instead
#01 variant: the frame split diagonally into a black half and a grey dithered half with a huge lowercase wordmark across the split, waving
Chunky 320x240 pixels, no anti-aliasing
styles.palette: One field colour, white text, a two- or three-tone logo. Aubergine about #2a0a3a with tan/gold logo; grey-green about #b9c9c0 with lighter cogs; lilac about #b080e0 with white/lavender checker; navy with green logo, red text and magenta rules. Hex values are read off screenshots, not sampled from the originals.
styles.typography: 8x8 or 16x16 bitmap capitals, square and wide, usually spaced one cell apart; hearts, stars and arrows as bullets; dashed rules made of hyphens. #5 uses the Amiga Topaz face according to a Pouet comment. Logos are drawn wordmarks, not fonts.
styles.motion: Text lines fade or type in one after another, hold, then swap to the next page (credits, greetings). The background loops: cogs turn, the checker floor spins. A Pouet comment on #09 lists a zoomed logo and scrolling text, so some of them do scroll.

references.what: Doom 3 Cracktro (Razor Crack Intro #09) on Pouet: aubergine field, tan logo, plaque, centred presents-text; comment lists zoomed logo, scrolling text, music
Same on Demozoo: 21 Jan 1997, code Hetero, logo Poise, music Spoon, blank version exists
Duke Nukem II Cracktro (Razor Crack Intro #10) on Demozoo: June 1997, code Hetero, music Technix, tag melon-dezign-inspired, blank template version noted
Quake 3 Cracktro (Razor Cracktro #7) on Demozoo: 20 Jan 1997, logo Dream Design, music M.C.MP, 320x240x8, Turbo Assembler
Same on Pouet: checker floor, fog, zooming text; called a remake of an Amiga intro by Paso
Razor cracktro #5 (with SAC): navy field, green outline logo, fading text writer, 'standard topaz' font
Razor Cracktro #01 (with SAC), Mar 1997: diagonal split, waved wordmark; conversion of an Aspect Amiga intro
Prestige's 1996 cracktro with the identical cog layout, called a Melon Dezign rip-off by commenters

styles.readme_translation: One SVG banner about 800x300. Flat colour fill; the project wordmark drawn as pixel rects at the top; a small plaque with the version; then three or four centred lines: project name letterspaced between two glyphs, a dashed rule, a presents-line with the release date, the tagline. One looping background effect behind the text (cogs are the cheap choice). Install command and links go in normal Markdown directly below.
styles.feasibility_notes: Pure shapes and CSS. Cogs: two or three gear paths with a rotate keyframe, opposite directions, fill a few percent lighter than the field. Text pages: groups with opacity keyframes and staggered delays. Pixel font: emit each glyph as rects or one path (no web fonts, and do not rely on a system monospace for the blocky look). A few KB, no filters. Only the rotating checker-floor variant is harder; use the chrome-spheres style for that.
styles.caveats: Do not copy any Razor wordmark, the 1911 name or the slogans. The compositions are conversions of Amiga intros, so treat cogs-behind-text and checker-floor-under-text as genre conventions and do not trace either. The game titles in these screens are template filler, not releases. Demozoo credits Hetero with code on #02, #03, #09, #10 and #11 but only with the font on #7, so 'coded by Hetero' is not confirmed for every number. Pale text on a pale field fails contrast without the dark outline.

styles.name: Plasma field with the logo embossed in it
styles.era: 1996-1997 on MS-DOS (Razor Crack Intro #02 and #03, code and graphics by Hetero); plasma as a backdrop survives into Windows cracktros (Hoodlum's LUCiD 4000th, Feb 2005). The effect itself is an early-90s demo staple.
styles.what_it_is: A full-screen single-hue plasma in which the group's wordmark appears as part of the plasma, as if pressed into it. Razor's two versions are the ones Pouet commenters single out, mostly for the tune and the little cartoon sprite. Demozoo notes that #02 picks its colour scheme at random on start, so the crimson and green seen in screenshots are two rolls of the same intro design.
visual_signature: The whole frame filled with soft, slowly crawling bands of one hue: crimson/magenta in the #02 screenshot, green in #03
Tall heavy serif capitals of the wordmark visible only as a lighter/darker displacement inside the plasma, tilted back in perspective so the letters lean away
Thin black letterbox bars top and bottom
A tiny cartoon sprite and a line of small white text in the top-left corner
Nothing else on screen: no frame, no starfield; text appears over the plasma in pages
Later descendant: plasma plus scroller plus chiptune as the default cracktro recipe (a commenter's dismissive summary of LUCiD 4000th)
styles.palette: Monochrome ramp from near-black through one hue to a pale tint: green about #001a00 to #7dff5a, crimson about #1a0010 to #ff5aa0. Pick the hue at random per build to echo the original's random palette.
styles.typography: Roman-style heavy serif capitals for the wordmark, rendered by the effect rather than drawn as a bitmap. Body text in a small white bitmap font.
styles.motion: Palette cycling: the field is computed once and the colour index shifts each frame, so the bands crawl while the shapes barely move; a slow sine drift bends the field (mechanism per Lode Vandevenne's tutorial, not observed in the cracktro itself).

references.what: Quake 2 Cracktro (1) [Razor Crack Intro #03] on Demozoo: 20 Jan 1997, code Hetero, music Spoon; another version has different music
Same on Pouet: green plasma screenshot; comment 'electronic plasma logotype in the background'
Razor Crack Intro #02 on Pouet, Dec 1996: crimson plasma screenshot; comments on plasma background, sprite and tune
Same on Demozoo ('Hetero Cracktro #02'): code and graphics Hetero, music Croaker; palette chosen at random on start
Hoodlum, LUCiD 4000th release (Feb 2005; code hitchhikr, graphics H2o, music Xerxes): commenter sums it up as plasma, scroller and chiptune
Lode Vandevenne's plasma tutorial: summed sines, cyclic palette, palette shift per frame

styles.readme_translation: A wide, short SVG strip (about 800x200) that is nothing but plasma with the project name embossed in it, letterboxed top and bottom. Tagline and install line sit underneath as ordinary Markdown. Works well as a thin strip above a text-only NFO block.
styles.feasibility_notes: Filter route (researcher tested in a Chromium , not re-tested): feTurbulence fractalNoise at low baseFrequency (about 0.012, 2 octaves) into feColorMatrix type=hueRotate with a SMIL animate on values 0 to 360, then feComponentTransfer with discrete tables to band it into one hue. This gives palette-cycling without script, but it is cloud noise rather than true sine plasma and the filter re-rasterises every frame, so keep the strip small. Logo: clip a second copy of the plasma with a phase offset inside the letter shapes, or use the letters as the map for feDisplacementMap. No-filter fallback that is cheaper and closer to sine plasma: four or five large radialGradient ellipses drifting on CSS keyframes with mix-blend-mode screen, with gradient stop colours keyframed. Safari and Firefox behaviour of the animated filter is unverified.
styles.caveats: Do not reuse Razor's wordmark or the corner sprites (commenters identify them as existing cartoon characters). Plasma is generic. Corrections to the submitted research: the Paradox 2000 cracktro cited as 'green plasma' is described by Pouet commenters as a blurred tunnel and has been moved to the tunnel style; the fire effect was removed from this style because no named PC cracktro using it was confirmed. Music for #03 is contested (Demozoo: Spoon; a Pouet commenter: Croaker; Demozoo says versions with different music exist), so it is not credited here. Full-frame colour cycling can be uncomfortable: cycle in 6 seconds or more and freeze under prefers-reduced-motion.

styles.name: Chrome spheres over a checkerboard
styles.era: Razor Cracktro #7 (DOS, Jan 1997) for the spinning checker floor; Hoodlum cracktro #1 (Windows, Nov 2004) and Skid Row's Streets of Moscow (May 2009) for checker floors under logos; Razor 1911's Deus Ex: Mankind Divided cracktro (Windows/Linux, 21 Nov 2016, code XT95) as the definitive version
styles.what_it_is: Mirror balls bouncing above an endless checker floor under a chrome logo: the scene's own in-joke for 'a demo'. Razor's 2016 cracktro plays it straight; rez (who says in the comment that he was not involved, though Pouet credits him with the font) invites everyone to post their 'no chrome spheres over checkerboard' meme, and the binary quoted in the comments is literally named after the checker. It reads as retro 3D instantly, even to people who never saw a cracktro.
visual_signature: Checkerboard floor in light and dark grey receding to a low horizon, squares foreshortened with distance
A loose row of five or six blue-tinted mirror spheres hovering just above the floor, each reflecting floor and sky, each with a soft shadow
A large italic chrome logo floating in the sky: steel-blue gradient faces, a lighter bevel, sharp diagonal cuts, slight perspective tilt
Sky as a smooth gradient that changes through the loop (Demozoo tag day-night-cycle; commenters praise the sun rising and setting); dusty mauve-grey in the Pouet screenshot
A scroller running small in the distance at floor level

Earlier cousins: lilac-and-white spinning checker with fog in Razor #7; bright blue-and-black checker under a bending blue logo with a fat yellow 3D scroller in Skid Row 2009; a spinning chessboard with balls morphing out of it in Hoodlum cracktro #1
styles.palette: Floor about #e8e8e8 and #4a4a4a; sky from a dusty pink or mauve at the horizon to blue above; chrome logo in steel blues (about #1b3a66, #5d8fd0, white highlight); spheres as blue-tinted mirrors. Night variant: same layout under a dark indigo sky.
styles.typography: Logo: wide italic capitals with diagonal cuts and a horizontal chrome break line (logo by Sprocket per both databases). Scroller: a bespoke bitmap font (credited separately to rez on Pouet).
styles.motion: Spheres bounce in a phase-shifted wave; the floor moves; the sky cycles slowly from day to night; the scroller crosses at the horizon; reflections follow. Commenters found the scroller slow.

references.what: Deus Ex: Mankind Divided Cracktro on Pouet: screenshot, credits (code Anat, font rez, logo sprocket, music dubmood and wasp), the chrome-spheres comments
Same on Demozoo: 21 Nov 2016, code XT95, music Dubmood and wasp, logo Sprocket, tag day-night-cycle
Hoodlum cracktro #1 on Pouet (Nov 2004): fake copper-split bars, rotating chessboard, balls morphing out of the checkerboard, metaballs
Same on Demozoo: 2 Nov 2004, code hitchhikr, graphics Alien, music Xerxes
Skid Row / Anti Nowhere League / Titan, Street of Moscow cracktro (May 2009): blue checker floor under a bending logo
Razor Cracktro #7 (Jan 1997): rotating checker floor with fog on a lilac field

styles.readme_translation: A 16:9-ish SVG hero (about 800x340): sky gradient, checker floor, a row of chrome spheres (one per feature, or one per letter of a short name), the project wordmark as the chrome logo in the sky, a one-line scroller at the horizon. Plain Markdown below for the install line and links.
styles.feasibility_notes: SVG has no perspective transform, so the generator projects the floor: emit it as 12-16 precomputed trapezoid rows of alternating quads. Sideways scroll is the cheap motion: each row group gets the same translateX keyframe with a per-row distance (inline CSS variable), clipped to the frame. Forward motion needs each row boundary animated to the next boundary's position with a colour swap at the wrap (SMIL animate on points), which is fiddlier. Spheres: radialGradient plus a clipped, squashed copy of checker and sky as the reflection, translateY keyframes with staggered delays; shadows are blurred ellipses scaling inversely. Chrome logo: linearGradient with a hard stop at the horizon line plus a light stroke; glyphs as paths. Day-night: keyframe the gradient stop colours. Well under 50 KB.
styles.caveats: Do not copy Razor's chrome wordmark or Sprocket's letterforms. Spheres on a checker floor is a shared scene cliche and free to use. The coder discrepancy in the submitted research is resolved: Pouet's 'Anat' and Demozoo's 'XT95' are the same person (rez's comment credits XT95, the quoted binary name contains XT95, and Demozoo lists XT95 as a member). Moving floors can cause motion discomfort: keep it slow and honour prefers-reduced-motion.

styles.name: Early DOS VGA loader: metal logo, gradient bars, one big scroller
styles.era: 1990-1993, MS-DOS VGA (mode 13h, 256 colours), often silent or AdLib; The Humble Guys, INC, USA/Fairlight, TRSI with The Dream Team, and Razor 1911's first PC intros (with Skillion)
styles.what_it_is: The first generation of graphical intros on the IBM PC, made before the platform had its own demoscene. Wikipedia credits The Humble Guys with bringing animated graphical intros, the NFO file and an intro-making tool to the PC. They are blunt next to Amiga work, which is the charm: a big metal logo, gradient bars, one line of oversized scrolling text. Razor's own first PC loaders (1990-93) belong here and are what the group looked like before the numbered series.
visual_signature: Group initials as a heavy framed plate: chrome letters with a blue-to-white 'sky' gradient in the upper half and a brown 'ground' gradient below, inside a grey bevelled frame (THG Lemmings, 1991)
Fat gold 3D serif capitals on black with specular highlights, and the group's full name set on a sine arc in small magenta capitals beneath (INC, 1992)
Background of nested concentric diamonds in one hue (electric blue on black), animated by palette rotation
Horizontal gradient bars in purple, orange and blue top and bottom, or passing through the logo as copper-style bars (INC Europe JOOP #2; a Pouet commenter calls THG's bars pseudo-3D copper bars)

Razor variant 1 (Silent Shadow, with Skillion): a red logo inside a rounded chrome capsule on deep-blue gradient bars, the partner's logo in a matching capsule below, and a scroller in very large red-to-orange gradient letters across the middle
Razor variant 2 (1992 loader, Maelstrom 1993): the name in red-to-yellow flame lettering with drips hanging off the bottom of each letter, over a starfield
Razor variant 3 (Battle Chess 4000, 1993): a huge bronze extruded serif wordmark with '1911' beneath, 'Another crack from' in small white type above, green scroller below
Single-line scroller in an oversized chunky font along the bottom edge; two crews' logos stacked when they co-released (USA over Fairlight, 1992)
styles.palette: Smooth VGA ramps: electric blue on black; gold (about #fff2a0 to #8a5a00); chrome (white, sky blue, brown); purple bars (about #ff7bff to #4a0a6a); flame (red #c00000 through orange to yellow). TRSI's Blues Brothers intro uses striped red-brown bars behind a gold skull with red eyes.
styles.typography: Logos are hand-drawn block or serif capitals with heavy bevel. Scrollers use oversized 16-32px bitmap fonts with squared counters and a vertical gradient fill.
styles.motion: Mostly palette cycling: the background pattern seems to pulse outward while no pixel moves. The scroller steps sideways a few pixels at a time (commenters call TRSI's 'choppy'). In the livelier ones the logo bounces with copper bars behind it, text rotates along a spline (JOOP #2), or the scroller rides an arch (Razor/Skillion Conan intro, 1991).

references.what: The Humble Guys, Lemmings Cracktro on Demozoo: 14 May 1991, code Jrok
Same on Pouet: blue diamond field, framed chrome plate, big white scroller; comments on the copper bars, no music, and that it remakes an Amiga intro by Mayhem
INC, Indiana Jones 4 cracktro (Pouet: Dec 1992; Demozoo: 6 Nov 1992): gold 3D letters, arc text, purple bars
INC Europe, JOOP #2 (Aug 1992): logo bouncing with copper bars behind it, spline text, scroller
Fairlight and USA, Wordtris (1992): two stacked logos and a scroller (Demozoo credits logo Red Devil, code The Necromancer)
TRSI and The Dream Team, Blues Brothers Cracktro (Demozoo: 12 Apr 1991): colour cycling and choppy scrolling
Razor 1911 and Skillion, Silent Shadow Cracktro (Pouet: Nov 1990; Demozoo: 1991; code Darwin, graphics Sector 9): capsule logos on blue bars, giant gradient scroller
Razor 1911 loader (starfield intro), 1992: flame-lettered logo over stars (Demozoo credits The French Mate with code and music)
Wikipedia on The Humble Guys: first NFO, first graphical PC intros, the THG IntroMaker

styles.readme_translation: SVG at about 800x250: black or deep-blue field with a palette-cycled diamond pattern or gradient bars, the project's initials as a framed metal plate (or a flame-lettered wordmark) in the centre, the full project name on an arc beneath, and one oversized gradient scroller along the bottom carrying tagline and greets. A text-only block can follow for the README body.
styles.feasibility_notes: Palette cycling maps onto keyframed fills on a set of nested polygons with staggered animation-delay, or animated gradient stops: no filters, tiny file. Plate: two or three linearGradients and inset strokes. Flame lettering: a vertical red-to-yellow gradient on glyph paths plus a few hand-placed drip shapes. Arc text: glyph paths placed along a precomputed arc (textPath works but depends on system fonts). Scroller: translateX on a long group with steps() timing to reproduce the choppy scroll. Distinct from the existing Amiga style by the static framed plate, the smooth VGA ramps and the step-scroll.
styles.caveats: Do not reuse THG, INC, USA, Fairlight, TRSI, Skillion or Razor logos or initials. Bevelled metal lettering, flame lettering and palette-cycled bars are generic. The THG plate itself is reported to be a remake of an Amiga intro. Dates differ between databases (INC Indy 4: Dec vs 6 Nov 1992; Silent Shadow: Nov 1990 vs 1991). A concentric pattern pulsing fast is a strobing risk: slow it down and provide a reduced-motion static frame.

styles.name: Win32 new old-school cracktro: metal logo, twister, sine scroller
styles.era: 2004-2011, Windows (DirectX/OpenGL, often 64k or less); Hoodlum, Deviance, Reloaded, Skid Row with Titan and Electric Druggies, Genesis with TRSI
styles.what_it_is: The mid-2000s revival in which demoscene coders (hitchhikr, the Titan people, anesthetic) and pixel artists (Alien^PDX, H2o, iks/irokos, bull) built deliberately old-school cracktros for ISO groups on modern hardware. It is what most people picture for a 2000s cracktro: a big airbrushed chrome or graffiti logo, a twisting column, a bouncing scroller and a chiptune. This entry now also absorbs the 'shiny' sub-look (logo on a mirror floor, lit relief) that was submitted as a separate style.
visual_signature: A large custom logo as the centrepiece: brushed-chrome 3D block letters (Reloaded), liquid-chrome script with drips (Deviance), gold wildstyle graffiti on black (Skidrow 2007), chrome-purple extruded capitals (Hoodlum Stronghold 2), grey-green metal (Genesis)

Twisters: a vertical bar that appears to twist like a wrung towel, one each side of the logo (Shrek 2 by Genesis/TRSI, praised as sine-twisters; Deviance 'Mission completed' is praised for its twister)

A scroller riding a sine wave or bending in 3D: pink on black (Hoodlum Stronghold 2), made of large LED-dot or cube letters along the bottom (Reloaded #4), a twisted 3D scroller that is famously unreadable (Hoodlum #3)
A centred text-writer block for release info and credits on a split dark-red background, with translucent red balls bouncing behind it (Deviance 'Old Skool')
Mirror floor: the chrome logo and a low-poly car standing on a dark glossy floor with their reflections (Reloaded #4); a rotating reflective box under the logo (Reloaded #2)
White-background variants: a pencil-sketch figure above small black type (Deviance 'Mission completed'), 3D letter sculptures and paper-tear transitions (Hoodlum #3)
3D starfield on black for the plain ones (Skidrow 2007)
Fake copper-split bars and a spinning chessboard as explicit Amiga nods (Hoodlum #1)
styles.palette: Black or near-black with one accent family: Deviance dark red and white; Reloaded steel grey with white LEDs; Hoodlum purple chrome with pink scroller; Skid Row gold on black (2007), purple and pink (2008), blue checker (2009); Genesis grey-green metal. The scroller usually carries the only bright colour.
styles.typography: The logo is always custom: chrome extrusion, graffiti with arrows and outlines, or script with drips. Body text in small white bitmap fonts; scroller fonts are big, rounded and gradient-filled or built from dots.
styles.motion: Twister rotates and bends on a sine; scroller letters ride a wave right to left; balls bounce; particles assemble into the logo left to right (Reloaded #4 per comments); text-writer types then wipes; starfield flies outward. Loops until a key is pressed.

references.what: Hoodlum cracktro #3 on Pouet (May 2005; code hitchhikr, graphics alien^PDX): white backgrounds, tetris break-up, paper tearing, twisted 3D scroller
Deviance 'Old Skool Cracktro' (Mar 2006; graphics H2o, music W.O.T.W.): bouncing translucent balls, text writer, chrome script logo
Deviance and Scoopex 'Mission completed' cracktro (Apr 2006; code anesthetic, graphics mrr and H2o): comments 'Best twistahr', 'Nice twist'
Reloaded Cracktro #4 with Titan (Pouet: Jan 2006; Demozoo: 29 Nov 2005; graphics alien^PDX): chrome block logo, particle-to-logo morph, car on glossy floor, LED scroller
Genesis and TRSI 'Shrek 2' cracktro (June 2004; code hitchhikr, graphics H2o, music estrayk): logo between two sine-twisters
Skidrow cracktro by Titan and Electric Druggies (Aug 2007; Demozoo title '911 First Responders', 13 Aug 2007): gold graffiti logo, 3D stars
Hoodlum and Titan, Stronghold 2 (Apr 2005; graphics bull): chrome-purple logo, z-shaded metaballs, pink sine scroll
Reloaded cracktro #2 with Titan (May 2005): rotating textured box under the logo
Paradox and Chemical Reaction cracktro (Pouet: May 2000): alien^PDX comments that he made 'the paradox logo with head bumpmap thing', the one named bump-mapped logo found

styles.readme_translation: SVG hero about 800x320 on near-black: the project wordmark as the metal logo in the upper half with a faded mirror reflection beneath it, a twister column at each side, a sine scroller along the bottom with the tagline, and a centred text-writer block cycling three pages (what it is, install line, credits). Links go underneath in Markdown.
styles.feasibility_notes: Twister: stack 40-60 thin horizontal slices, each holding two or three coloured rects whose x and width follow one shared keyframe with a negative animation-delay proportional to the row; plain CSS, no filters. Sine scroller: per-letter groups with staggered translateY keyframes inside a parent translating left; keep it to one short line. Chrome logo: layered linearGradients with a hard horizon stop, an inner highlight stroke and a drop shadow; real airbrush texture is not achievable, so aim for clean vector chrome. Mirror floor: a <use> of the logo flipped with scale(1,-1) under a linear-gradient mask. Optional moving light: feSpecularLighting over a blurred alpha height map with an fePointLight whose x is animated by SMIL; the researcher saw it render in Chromium but did not confirm the light moving, so treat it as unverified and keep a plain gradient-sweep fallback (an animated highlight band clipped to the letters). Glyphs must be paths. About 40-60 KB.
styles.caveats: The logos are the credited artists' signature work: describe and link, never trace. Group names and wordmarks are off limits. Twisters, sine scrollers, mirror floors and bouncing balls are common property. Pouet files the 2007-2011 Skid Row cracktros under the same group entry as the Amiga-era group; Demozoo credits Razor founder Sector 9 with graphics on Skid Row's 2008 Gene Troopers, but lineage is still not something I confirmed. The 2009 Genesis cracktro's chrome skull is described by commenters as a Terminator theme: film imagery, not to be imitated. An unbroken sine scroller is hard to read; keep essential text in the static block.

styles.name: Skinned rip installer: INSTALL / NFO / MUSIC / EXIT
styles.era: 1997-2004, Windows (Class and Myth game-rip installers); a DOS precedent in Razor's 1997 'Arnie 3' cracktro, a fake GUI window converted from an Amiga trainer
styles.what_it_is: Rip groups cut games down to small packages and shipped their own installer, which doubled as the intro: a custom-shaped window with a logo sign, three or four buttons, an info viewport and a chiptune playlist. Wikipedia describes Class's rips, its custom installation software and its rivalry with Myth; Pouet commenters remember the Class installers mainly for the Maktone tunes and complain about hearing them recycled. It is a different object from the keygen dialog: no serial field, a release menu instead.
visual_signature: A non-rectangular window skin floating on the desktop: a sci-fi gadget with pipes, cables and a riveted blue viewport (Class 'orcus' installer, 2002), an isometric slab in translucent teal with the group name extruded on top (Myth 4-02)
The group name as a lit sign: orange-to-yellow capitals in a red bevelled frame bolted to the top-left of the gadget (Class orcus)
A short button column or row, always some subset of INSTALL, NFO, MUSIC, EXIT/QUIT, plus a small music on/off toggle

A viewport for release info with one modest effect inside it: a rotating, morphing 3D dot scroller (orcus), rising bubbles and a rotating dot logo on navy with cyan frame lines (Class 'bubbles', 2001), faint drifting specks (Myth)
A credits strip along the bottom edge of the window naming code, graphics and music

DOS precedent: a grey pseudo-GUI screen with the logo as a title bar, a text pane on the left and a vertical button stack reading Release, Credits, Greets, Contact, Exit on the right (Razor Arnie 3, 1997)
styles.palette: Per skin: navy and white with cyan frame lines (bubbles); steel grey and blue with an orange neon sign (orcus); teal monochrome (Myth 4-02); flat greys (Arnie 3).
styles.typography: Button labels in small capitals, bitmap or monospace; info text in a fixed-width pixel font; the logo as a custom sign.
styles.motion: Low key: the viewport effect loops, the dot scroller rotates and morphs, text appears as a pixel cloud and resolves (bubbles installer per comments), a progress bar fills during install. In the originals the music is the main event.

references.what: Class 'orcus installer' on Pouet (2002): skinned gadget window; comments on the dot scroller and the Buzz, Maktone and Purple Motion tunes
Same on Demozoo: code Orcus, graphics Andrius; note that the title shown may be a template with no real release behind it
Class 'bubbles installer' (Aug 2001; code and graphics zooperdan, music Maktone): 3D bubbles, rotating dot logo, pixel-cloud text
Myth installer 4-02 (2002; graphics and music kenet, music med): teal isometric slab with INSTALL MUSIC .NFO EXIT
Class installer skinned as a handheld console (Feb 1999; graphics ATM, music Maktone): cited only as an example of what not to copy
Razor 1911 Arnie 3 Cracktro (DOS, May 1997; code Hetero, music W.O.T.W. per Demozoo): fake GUI with a button stack; conversion of a Supplex Amiga trainer per comments
Wikipedia on Class: rips, installers, rivalry with Myth, 1,234 releases, endtro on 9 Jan 2004

styles.readme_translation:
SVG of a shaped installer window: logo sign, a viewport showing project name, version and one-line description with a small looping effect, a progress bar that fills and resets, and a button column. Links do not work inside an , so repeat the buttons directly below as a row of real Markdown links ([ INSTALL ] [ NFO ] [ DOCS ] [ EXIT ]) or as a text-only 
 menu with anchors; each button maps to a README section.
styles.feasibility_notes: All vector. Window silhouette as one path with gradient fill and inner bevel strokes; viewport is a clipPath holding circles on a translateY keyframe (bubbles) or a ring of dots whose positions are precomputed per frame and animated with SMIL values lists (dot scroller); progress bar is a rect with a width keyframe using steps(). 15-40 KB depending on the dot count.
styles.caveats: Do not imitate real hardware or brand trade dress: the 1999 Class installer reproduces a commercial handheld console including the maker's logo, and its music is a remix of a well-known game theme; neither may be copied. Do not reuse Class, Myth or Razor wordmarks. A shaped window with INSTALL/NFO/MUSIC/EXIT is generic. A MUSIC button promises sound a README cannot deliver: drop it or link it to a tracker module. Demozoo titles the 1999 Class installer after the game it shipped with and dates it 20 Feb 1999.

styles.name: Text-mode poster installer (Razor 1911, 2024-26)
styles.era: May 2024 onward, Windows; Razor 1911 game installers with code by Black Panther, graphics by Goto80 and music by Dubmood, plus the text-art passages of the 2026 anniversary demo Razor1911
styles.what_it_is: Razor's current house look, and the one most directly usable as plain text: each installer is a single character-cell poster in two or three flat colours, with the game title and the group name built as enormous block letters that fill the frame, and two small buttons. A Pouet commenter credits these with taking cracktro style somewhere new 'like Melon Dezign used to'. The same vocabulary (PETSCII, ANSI, ASCII, BBS file lists) runs through the group's 40th-anniversary demo, which won the PC demo competition at Revision 2026.
visual_signature: Title and group name as giant letters built from solid character cells with maze-like notches, packed edge to edge so the lettering is the whole composition (Red Dead Redemption 2 installer: orange letters on a tan field inside a rope-pattern border)

Strict two- or three-colour schemes per screen: tan/orange/brown; blue/yellow/red with a lattice of yellow triangles above a red band (GTA III); lavender blocks on steel blue (Half-Life 2); lime and dark green checker borders on black (Little Kitty Big City)
A 1-bit variant: a white oval porthole on black with dithered edges, a maroon block logo across it and the title in small red monospace (Dungeons of Hinterberg)
An outline-ASCII variant: the logo drawn in thin green or cyan-and-purple slashes and underscores on black, with a leetspeak 'another one from...' line above (Galacticare, Magical Delicacy)
Exactly two controls, tiny, bottom right: INSTALL and QUIT/EXIT, sometimes in brackets, sometimes as cells in a bottom bar reading group | title | install | quit (Half-Life 2)
An install-path field drawn as an inverse-video bar (Magical Delicacy)
No gradients, no anti-aliasing, no 3D: every shape sits on the character grid
styles.palette: Two or three flat colours per screen, different every time: tan #e0b080 with orange #e08040; royal blue with yellow and brick red; black with lime; black with white and maroon. Choose one pair per project.
styles.typography: All lettering is built from character cells: full blocks and half blocks for the giant letters, a small 8x8 monospace for labels. The giant letters are drawn, not typed: letterforms interlock and share strokes.
styles.motion: Not observed; screenshots only. The installers are interface screens with music, so assume little beyond a cursor, a progress indication and button states.

references.what: Dungeons of Hinterberg Installer on Demozoo: 18 July 2024, code Black Panther, graphics Goto80, music Dubmood
Same on Pouet: 1-bit porthole screenshot; comments praising it as something different in modern cracktros
Grand Theft Auto III Definitive Edition Installer (Demozoo: 1 Nov 2024): blue/yellow/red lattice and block lettering
Red Dead Redemption 2 Installer (May 2024): orange maze lettering in a rope border
Half Life 2 20th Anniversary Edition Installer (Nov 2024): lavender blocks, four-cell bottom bar
Galacticare Installer (May 2024): outline ANSI logo, leetspeak header, italic INSTALL / QUIT
Magical Delicacy Installer (July 2024): green outline ASCII logo, inverse-video path field
Razor1911, the anniversary demo on Demozoo: 5 Apr 2026, 1st in PC demo at Revision 2026; tags scene-history; ANSI/ASCII and PETSCII graphics credited

styles.readme_translation: The header is one poster: the project name as giant block letters filling an 80-column <pre> (full block, half blocks and shade characters), a one-line title strip, and two bracketed links at the bottom right, [ INSTALL ] and [ DOCS ], which are real links inside the <pre>. For colour, ship the same grid as a static SVG of rects in two or three flat colours and keep the <pre> version as the alt text or a fallback below.
styles.feasibility_notes: Text route: the generator lays the name out on a cell grid and prints U+2588, U+2580, U+2584, U+258C, U+2590 and U+2591-2593; GitHub's monospace renders these cleanly in a code block, monochrome, at 80 columns or fewer. SVG route: one rect per filled cell (merge runs into wider rects), two or three fills, shape-rendering crispEdges; a few KB and pixel-exact. Optional motion: a blinking cursor and a progress bar made of cells stepping with steps() timing.
styles.caveats: Do not copy Goto80's letterforms or compositions, the Razor name or block logos, or the game titles and their marks (several of these screens restyle a game publisher's logo). What is reusable is the method: giant interlocking cell lettering in two flat colours with two tiny buttons. It overlaps the existing C64 and ANSI styles in raw material but not in layout (no boot text, no BBS menu). One screen in the series is a cartoon illustration rather than text mode, so the series is not uniformly character-cell. Block characters can show hairline gaps in some fonts; test on GitHub mobile.

styles.name: Trainer menu: F-key toggles under a logo
styles.era: 1993-2006: DOS trainers by Razor 1911 (1993-94); Windows trainers by Hoodlum (2004-05), Deviance (2005), FANAiON with Titan (2005) and Razor (2006)
styles.what_it_is: A trainer patches a running game to give cheats, and its screen is a cracktro with a job to do: a logo on top and a list of function-key toggles underneath. It is the most list-shaped screen in the family, which makes it the easiest to turn into something useful, and the VU bars in the 1993 Razor one are the natural visual stand-in for the music a README cannot play.
visual_signature: A logo at the top, smaller than in a cracktro: a wordmark whose letters each carry a different rainbow gradient (Razor 1993, logo by Pal per Demozoo), a green-and-yellow graffiti piece (Hoodlum 2005), a grey-teal stone-textured logo (Razor Gothic 3, 2006)
A title block: 'presents', the game name with a '+N' option count, 'trained by' and the author
The list: one row per function key, key name at the left, effect at the right, sometimes ending in a bracketed [OFF] state (Razor Gothic 3)
A full-width magenta highlight bar on the selected row (Razor Alien Breed +11)
Two stubby yellow VU-meter bars in the bottom corners (same trainer)
An instruction line at the bottom saying which keys work in-game and how to continue

Windows-era additions around the centred list: a faceted green polyhedron (Hoodlum #3), a pink vector star drifting on a purple-to-blue gradient (Deviance, Hoodlum Bugdom 2), a sine scroller, or the group name spelled in shaded dots (FANAiON)
styles.palette: Black background in most. Razor 1993: rainbow logo, white list, magenta bar, yellow meters. Hoodlum 2005: acid green and yellow logo, white list. Deviance 2005 and FANAiON 2005: purple-to-blue gradient field with white text and pink accents. Razor's 1994 Pinball Fantasies trainer is just a dark-red serif logo over grey text.
styles.typography: Monospaced bitmap capitals so the key column and the description column align; fixed tabs or leader dots between them. Logos are custom.
styles.motion: The highlight bar steps from row to row; VU bars jump; logo colours cycle; in the later ones a scroller runs under the list and the side object rotates (a commenter on Hoodlum's notes parallax stars, a rotating vector star and a sine scroll).

references.what: Razor Trainer Alien Breed +11 on Pouet (Nov 1993): rainbow logo, F-key list, magenta bar, yellow VU bars
Same on Demozoo: 4 Nov 1993; menu code Lithium, logo Pal, font Poise, trainer Red Wizard
Hoodlum trainer #3 (Apr 2005; graphics H2o): F-key toggles, green polyhedron; the comment asking why modern crack intros have no glenz
Razor 1911 Gothic 3 Trainer (Oct 2006; code blkpanther, graphics kenet, music dubmood): list with [OFF] states
Deviance Trainer (Sep 2005; code SIRIaX and aLpHa oNe): purple gradient, pink star, centred toggle list, scroller
Hoodlum Bugdom 2 trainer (Nov 2004; graphics angelDawn): parallax stars, vector star, sine scroll, called an old-skool trainer menu
FANAiON and Titan, Stronghold 2 +6 trainer (Apr 2005; code and graphics zooperdan, music xerxes): F-key list over dot lettering
Razor Pinball Fantasies trainer (DOS, Jan 1994): red serif logo over grey instruction text

styles.readme_translation: The list is the README's feature or command table. Above the fold: a small SVG with the logo, colour cycling and VU bars; then a text-only <pre> block, for example (my own illustration): 'F1  WATCH MODE ............ [ON ]' / 'F2  DRY RUN ............... [OFF]' / 'F3  VERBOSE LOGS .......... [ON ]', each key mapping to a CLI flag or feature, with links on the descriptions. A '+7' after the project name gives the feature count.
styles.feasibility_notes: The list works as plain monospace text in a code block (links work inside <pre>), so the essential part needs no SVG. Animated version in one SVG: a highlight rect stepping down the rows with steps() timing, a few rects on scaleY keyframes with different durations for VU bars, a per-letter gradient logo whose stops are keyframed. Under 10 KB.
styles.caveats: Do not reuse any group logo or name. The F-key list is generic. Replace cheat wording with the project's own features and avoid implying the README does anything to other software. If ON/OFF states are shown, make them match real defaults or label them as decoration. Commenters note the Deviance trainer borrowed its font and tune from another group's work without credit: a reminder to credit sources.

styles.name: Pencil on paper: the cracktro that draws itself
styles.era: 1997-1998, MS-DOS; Razor 1911 Cracktro #11 and 'Razor is back (Postal fix)' with SAC, code and graphics by Hetero, music by Argon (Demozoo)
styles.what_it_is: A cracktro with no logo bitmap and no scroller: a shaded pencil lies on blue paper at the end of a chalk-white line drawing and a handwritten message. Pouet commenters love #11 for the comic style and the tune (one calls it the greatest cracktro of all time) and point at its antecedents: one says the authors must have watched 'Paper', another calls it a Crystal rip-off 'in a nice way'.
visual_signature: Mid-blue paper with a visible fine woven grain
White chalk-like line art, slightly rough and broken, as if dragged over the grain
A shaded pencil with a green barrel and a yellow band lying diagonally, its point touching the end of the newest line
A large cartoon figure drawn in outline only, no fills, with speed lines
A handwritten message in the same line: uneven baseline, mixed case, a dash, an underline
Nothing else on screen: no bars, no starfield, no frame
styles.palette: Paper blue about #2b5fa8 with darker grain; line about #e8f0ff at partial opacity; pencil greens about #3cb043 and #1d6b2a with a yellow #ffd400 band. Re-skins that keep the idea: white chalk on blackboard green, graphite on cream.
styles.typography: Handwriting, not a font: single-stroke letters with wobble; the group name appears only as handwriting.
styles.motion: Inferred from the still and the concept: the pencil travels along each stroke and the line appears behind it; the finished drawing holds, then the page clears for the next one.

references.what: Quake 2 Cracktro (2) [Razor Cracktro #11] on Pouet: blue paper, outline cartoon, green pencil; comments on the comic style, 'Paper' and Crystal
Same on Demozoo: Hetero code and graphics, music 'CocoPops V1.2 (Yum!)' by Argon; dated 20 Jan 1997 there, Feb 1998 on Pouet
'Razor is back (postal fix)' on Pouet, Sept 1997: handwritten message and running figure in the same style
Same on Demozoo: 24 Sep 1997, Hetero code and graphics, Argon music, spread with a fix for a game

styles.readme_translation: SVG banner about 800x260: textured blue paper, the project name handwritten by a travelling pencil, then a small original line drawing relevant to the project (a gear, a terminal, your own mascot), then one handwritten tagline. Holds a few seconds and loops. The real README text follows in Markdown.
styles.feasibility_notes: The drawing technique is easy and standard: each path gets stroke-dasharray equal to its length and a stroke-dashoffset keyframe, chained with animation-delay (the researcher tested this in a Chromium ). The pencil follows the same path with SMIL animateMotion timed to match. What pushes it to medium is the input: handwriting needs single-line glyph paths, so the generator must ship a stroke font (a Hershey-style single-stroke set) and compute path lengths, because outline fonts cannot be 'written'. Paper grain: a tiny repeating pattern, or one static feTurbulence at low opacity (static filters cost nothing per frame). Rough chalk edge: a static feDisplacementMap on the strokes. 10-30 KB.
styles.caveats: The original drawings are of a famous newspaper-strip character (a commenter names him); draw an original subject, never an existing cartoon character. Do not copy the message wording or the Razor name. Self-drawing line art on paper is free to use and predates this cracktro according to the comments. The two databases disagree on #11's date by a year. White on mid-blue only passes contrast at thick stroke widths: keep strokes 3px or more at display size, and repeat the project name as real text below the image.

styles.name: Fake desktop takeover
styles.era: Fairlight, Quake 3 Arena cracktro (Windows 9x, 2 Dec 1999; code Exeron, music Joule, logo Lek, font Maniac per Demozoo) and Razor 1911, D-cracktro 02 (Windows, 7 Nov 2025; code Anat and Dubmood, graphics Goto80)
styles.what_it_is: A cracktro that pretends to be, or takes over, the user's own desktop. Fairlight's 1999 version shows a teal Win9x desktop with the group's name as the wallpaper and the release info in an ordinary-looking dialog; a Pouet commenter recalls running it and finding the wallpaper changed, the icons gone and a small window on screen. Razor's 2025 version captures the real desktop as a texture (confirmed in the comments) and shatters it like glass to show a black void with a red wireframe sheet behind.
visual_signature: Flat teal desktop with the group name as a huge darker-teal lowercase wordmark across the top, like a watermark wallpaper
Two desktop icons with labels stacked at the top left
A grey taskbar along the bottom with a start button at the left and a clock at the right
One small dialog in the centre: grey 3D-bevelled frame, navy title bar with three caption buttons, and a teal-green panel inside holding the release info in small monospace text
2025 variant: whatever desktop was on screen cracks into a dozen large angular shards radiating from an off-centre impact point; the middle is a jagged black hole
Through the hole: a red wireframe grid sheet, gently warped, with a tiny group credit beside it
No logo art beyond the wallpaper wordmark: the joke is that it looks like nothing special
styles.palette: Period system colours: teal #008080, dialog grey #c0c0c0 with white and dark-grey bevels, navy title bar #000080, white caption text. Shatter variant: black void, red wireframe about #d0202a, thin pale crack lines.
styles.typography: A small system UI sans for captions and icon labels; the wallpaper wordmark in a heavy lowercase sans; dialog contents in a monospaced pixel font.
styles.motion: 1999: essentially static, text in the dialog with a chiptune. 2025 (from the still and comments): shards separate and the wireframe undulates while a scroller runs; a commenter found the scroll hard to read in places.

references.what: Fairlight Quake 3 Arena cracktro on Pouet: fake-desktop screenshot; the changed-wallpaper comment
Same on Demozoo: 2 Dec 1999, credits, blank version exists
Razor 1911 D-cracktro 02 on Pouet (Nov 2025): broken-glass screenshot; comment that the desktop is taken as a D3D11 texture
Same on Demozoo: 7 Nov 2025; code Anat and Dubmood, graphics Goto80, music covers by Dubmood and MASTER BOOT RECORD

Razor Logo 01 (Feb 2009; code replay, graphics sprocket): in the Pouet screenshot a chrome logo sits over a stock OS wallpaper, an earlier desktop gag if it is drawn over the live desktop (not confirmed)

styles.readme_translation: SVG of a small period desktop: the project name as the wallpaper watermark, icons named after the repo's real files (README, LICENSE, src), a taskbar whose clock shows the version number, and one dialog whose title bar is the project name and whose body is the install command and tagline. Optional second state: the desktop cracks and a wireframe shows through. Links and the copyable command repeat below in Markdown.
styles.feasibility_notes: Rectangles, 1px bevel lines and short text: the easiest style here to make pixel-accurate, and real <text> in a generic sans is acceptable because a system UI font is exactly the look (still fix sizes and test widths). Animation: a blinking caret and paging text in the dialog (opacity keyframes), a clock that ticks with steps(). Shatter variant: precompute 10-15 shard polygons as clipPaths over <use> copies of the desktop group and give each a small translate/rotate keyframe; the wireframe is a polyline grid with SMIL-animated points. Under 40 KB with the shards.
styles.caveats: Do not use any operating-system vendor's logos, flag, wordmark or real icons; draw a generic period desktop with your own icons and a plain start button (the 2025 screenshot shows a real OS wallpaper only because that is what was on the uploader's screen). Do not reuse the Fairlight wordmark. A header that imitates an OS dialog must not be mistakable for a real system prompt: keep it decorative and never word it as a security or installer warning. The fake-desktop idea itself is free to reuse.

styles.name: BIOS setup hijack: the firmware screen that starts misbehaving
styles.era: Razor 1911, CMOS Cosmos (Windows, 29 Nov 2025; by Anat, Dubmood, Flopine, Goto80 and zabutom), 1st in the combined demo/intro competition at Compusphere 2025. A dentro rather than a cracktro, but it is current Razor and the look is a PC-only one.
styles.what_it_is: A demo staged inside a PC BIOS setup screen: the familiar navy text-mode page with a double-line frame and a key legend, whose main panel then fills with text-mode effects. Pouet commenters single out 'the old school CMOS screens' and 'the BIOS part', one wishes for a whole demo inside those UI constraints, another calls it the perfect prank for an unlocked computer. Demozoo lists it as nominated for Best Direction at the Meteoriks 2026 and tags it with an epilepsy warning.
visual_signature: Full-screen navy blue text mode with a single centred title line at the top reading like a setup utility name and copyright
A white double-line box-drawing frame divided into a large upper panel and a shallow lower area
A vertical divider down the middle of the upper panel, as in a two-column setup menu

Inside the upper panel, the effect: rows of horizontal bars shading from orange at top and bottom to magenta in the middle, with a diamond-shaped cluster of blue arrow glyphs pointing outward from the centre line
A key legend in small white text in the lower area: a quit key and a save-and-exit key at the left, arrow keys and 'select item' at the right
A one-line hint in yellow, centred in its own box at the very bottom
Everything stays on the 80x25 character grid, even the effect
styles.palette: Navy #0000a8 field, white frame and legend, yellow hint text, red for a selection bar (standard setup-screen convention); the effect adds orange-to-magenta bars and blue arrows.
styles.typography: The PC 8x16 text-mode font throughout: box-drawing double lines for the frame, arrow and triangle glyphs used as effect pixels, capitals for menu items.
styles.motion: Not observed beyond one still. Comments describe a BIOS screen that lingers and then takes off, a 'dot ball' part and strong music sync; assume a static menu first, then character-cell effects inside the panel.

references.what: CMOS Cosmos on Pouet: setup-screen screenshot; comments on the CMOS/BIOS screens, the dot ball, the concept
Same on Demozoo: 29 Nov 2025, 1st at Compusphere 2025, tags dentro and epilepsy-warning, Meteoriks nomination

styles.readme_translation: A setup menu is already a table of contents. Text-only version: a <pre> box with a title line, two columns of menu items that are real links to README sections (for example FEATURES SETUP, INTEGRATED TOOLS, LOAD DEFAULTS as quick start, SAVE & EXIT as license), a key legend and a one-line hint that is the tagline. SVG version: the same screen in navy, white and yellow with a red selection bar stepping through the items, after which the upper panel is taken over by a character-cell effect. Use either, or the SVG above the <pre>.
styles.feasibility_notes: Text route: box-drawing double lines (U+2554 family) and plain capitals in a code block, 78 columns; links inside <pre> work. SVG route: a navy rect, the frame as crisp 2px double strokes (or glyph paths), text as pixel-font paths or rects, a red rect stepping between rows with steps() timing, a blinking cursor. The takeover effect stays cheap because it lives on an 80x25 grid: rows of rects whose fills are keyframed with per-row delays for the colour bars, and a few dozen glyph shapes switched on and off with opacity keyframes for the diamond. 10-30 KB.
styles.caveats: Do not copy the title line: the screenshot's heading names a real BIOS vendor and copyright notice, which must not be reproduced; write a generic 'SETUP UTILITY' line with the project's own name. Do not copy Razor's effect designs. A blue setup screen is a generic convention and free to use. Only one still was seen, so the motion description is second-hand. The original carries an epilepsy warning: keep any takeover effect slow and low-contrast and freeze it under prefers-reduced-motion. It is close in spirit to the existing phosphor-terminal style but differs in colour, layout (menu, not shell) and the takeover idea.

styles.name: Neon cube field: the rez-era Razor look
styles.era: 2010-2012, Windows; Razor 1911 cracktros and 64k intros coded by rez with music by Dubmood (The Settlers 7 cracktro, 27 Apr 2010; StarCraft 2 cracktro, 31 July 2010; Insert No Coins, 2 Oct 2010; The Scene Is Dead, 8 Apr 2012). A DOS ancestor exists in Razor Crack Intro #13.
styles.what_it_is: When Razor's demo section came back around 2010 it had a consistent look: fields of glowing rainbow cubes and glenz shapes, a pixel logo, scanlines and a Dubmood chiptune. Insert No Coins won the 64k competition at Main 2010 and the public-choice award at the Scene.org Awards; The Scene Is Dead placed third in PC 64k at Revision 2012. For many people this is 'the Razor 1911 one'. The rainbow-cubes idea is older than rez's use of it: the undated DOS Crack Intro #13 already shows a 9x7 grid of cubes, one hue per cube.
visual_signature: Hundreds of small cubes in a regular grid, each a different hue, so the field reads as a continuous rainbow ramp
The field bent into a tunnel, a rolling wave landscape, or a wall seen in perspective (the four panels of the Insert No Coins screenshot)
Glow on everything against near-black
A segmented, LCD-like pixel wordmark pinned to the top centre of the frame (logo by iLKke on Insert No Coins)
Rows of small translucent glenz polyhedra ordered by hue behind a rainbow block-letter logo, under horizontal scanlines (Settlers 7 cracktro)
Text as three-dimensional ASCII characters and a rotating 3D ASCII logo, a starfield with a cube, turning cogs and a sine scroller (StarCraft 2 cracktro, per comments)
CRT treatment: scanlines, vignette and phosphor glow, which several commenters found overdone (The Scene Is Dead)
DOS ancestor: flat-shaded rainbow cubes in a grid with the logo running vertically down the left edge (#13)
styles.palette: Near-black background with a full-spectrum hue ramp at high saturation across the field. The Scene Is Dead narrows to amber, cyan and magenta on black (Vivian Voss's write-up).
styles.typography: A pixel wordmark built from segments; body text in a small square bitmap font in white or pale cyan; extruded ASCII characters in the StarCraft 2 cracktro; text-writer delivery.
styles.motion: From comments and stills: camera travel through or over the cube field, cubes rippling in a wave, glenz objects spinning, text typing on, scanlines fixed on top. Not watched.

references.what: Insert No Coins on Demozoo: 2 Oct 2010, 1st at Main 2010, code rez, logo Ilkke, music Dubmood, public-choice award, source available
Insert No Coins on Pouet: four-panel screenshot (cube tunnel, rainbow wave landscape)
StarCraft 2 cracktro on Pouet (July 2010; code rez, graphics kenet, music W.O.T.W. with a Dubmood remix): comments on the 3D ASCII, starfield with cube, sine scroller, cogs
The Settlers 7 Cracktro on Pouet (Apr 2010): rainbow logo over rows of glenz shapes; the ACiD logo dispute in the comments
Same on Demozoo: 27 Apr 2010, code and graphics rez, music Dubmood (and zabutom, uncredited)
The Scene Is Dead on Pouet (Apr 2012, 3rd in PC 64k at Revision): comments on the CRT filter
Vivian Voss on The Scene Is Dead: CRT post-processing, amber/cyan/magenta on black, rez and Dubmood
Razor Crack Intro #13 (DOS): grid of rainbow cubes with a vertical logo; undated on Pouet

styles.readme_translation: SVG hero about 800x340 on black: an isometric field of small cubes rippling in a sine wave with the hue sweeping across it, the project wordmark as a segmented pixel logo at the top centre, one line of text typing on, scanlines over everything. Install line and links below in Markdown.
styles.feasibility_notes: A fixed isometric view is practical: emit a 16x8 grid of cubes (three polygons each: top, left and right faces at three lightness levels of the cube's hue), give every cube the same translateY keyframe with a negative delay derived from its grid position so a wave travels across, and set hues statically by column. About 400 polygons and one keyframe, 60-120 KB; reduce to 12x6 to halve it. Scanlines: a 2px pattern overlay. Vignette: a radial gradient. Glow: a single static blurred duplicate layer at most; an animated blur over 400 moving shapes is too expensive. The camera fly-through and cube tunnel of the originals would need per-frame geometry and exceed the budget: not possible as such.
styles.caveats: Do not copy Razor's pixel wordmark (a credited artist's logo) or the name. The rainbow block logo in the Settlers 7 cracktro is, according to Pouet comments by ACiD's radman and by rez, an ACiD text-art logo by JED from 1996 reused with an altered signature, which drew an objection: a concrete example of why borrowed logos must be avoided. Cube fields, glenz and scanlines are generic. #13's date is unconfirmed (none on Pouet; Demozoo says 1994, which sits oddly with the 1996-98 numbering). Wow lowered from 5 to 4 because the buildable version is a static-camera cube wave without bloom. Saturated rainbow motion across the full width is tiring: keep amplitude and speed low, freeze under prefers-reduced-motion, and test scrolling on a phone.

styles.name: Vector objects: wireframe, glenz, vector balls, dot scroller, metaballs
styles.era: Effect vocabulary from early-90s demos; in PC cracktros 1998-2010 (Razor #12 beta on DOS; Titan with Backlash, FANAiON, Electric Druggies/Skid Row, Class, Hoodlum and Razor on Windows)
styles.what_it_is: The family of effects where one geometric object rotates in the middle of the screen while the text does the talking. Wikipedia's demo-effect article lists them under vector graphics and describes glenz as partly see-through models with a diamond-like look. Sceners are openly sentimental about it: a Pouet commenter on a 2005 Hoodlum trainer asks why contemporary crack intros have no glenz. Metaballs, submitted separately, are folded in here as the 'liquid' member of the same family.
visual_signature: Wireframe: a solid drawn as thin single-colour lines, rotating faintly behind huge white block capitals zooming past on a cyan field (Razor #12 beta), or in front of concentric blue circles zooming inward with ASCII text scrolling up (Titan and Backlash, 2005)

Glenz: small translucent polyhedra in rows, tinted in rainbow order (Razor Settlers 7), or pink-and-purple crystals drifting over a purple checker tunnel with a ribbon logo (Electric Druggies and Skid Row, Gene Troopers)
Vector balls and dot lettering: shaded dots arranged into shapes or into the group name (FANAiON and Titan trainer; commenters credit a dot effect and 'vectorballs')
Dot scroller: a band of text made of points, wrapped around a rotating 3D shape that morphs (Class 'orcus' installer)
Metaballs: three z-shaded blobs fusing and separating under a chrome logo (Hoodlum and Titan, Stronghold 2), or balls morphing up out of a checkerboard (Hoodlum cracktro #1)
Flat blobs: soft olive-gold discs drifting behind a khaki logo and white text-writer lines (SAC Blizzard cracktro, 1999; a commenter guesses 'fake 2d metaballs')
Background kept plain so the object reads: flat colour, slow gradient or starfield
styles.palette: Wireframe: one line colour on a flat field (white on cyan, cyan on black). Glenz: white plus one tint at about 50 percent opacity, brighter where faces overlap. Vector balls: one or two ball colours with a white highlight. Metaballs: one saturated colour with depth shading.
styles.typography: Not font-led: text is whatever the host cracktro uses. Razor #12 beta uses huge white block capitals; the Backlash cracktro uses ASCII text.
styles.motion: Continuous rotation on two or three axes at different speeds; objects bounce or drift on a sine path; dot objects morph between shapes; glenz faces change tint as they turn; blobs orbit, merge and pinch apart.

references.what: Wikipedia, Demo effect: vector graphics list including glenz ('partially see-through models with a diamond-like look'); chunky-pixel list including metaballs and bump mapping
Razor Cracktro #12 beta (DOS, Mar 1998): wireframe object behind zooming text on cyan
Razor 1911 Settlers 7 Cracktro (2010): rows of glenz shapes ('Love those glenzes')
Electric Druggies and Skid Row, Gene Troopers (May 2008): glenz cubes and checkerboard
Titan and Backlash cracktro (Oct 2005; code red, graphics bull, music SaxxonPike): zooming circles, rotating wireframe figure, ASCII text scrolling up
FANAiON and Titan Stronghold 2 +6 trainer (Apr 2005): dot effect and vector balls
Hoodlum and Titan, Stronghold 2 (Apr 2005): 'z-shaded metablobs'
Superior Art Creations, Blizzard Cracktro (DOS, Mar 1999): blobs behind a khaki logo

styles.readme_translation: The centrepiece of a minimal header: one rotating wireframe or glenz solid (or a trio of metaballs) at the left or centre, project name and tagline set beside it in a pixel or mono face, on a flat field. It also drops into other styles here: a glenz object beside the trainer menu, or in the viewport of the installer.
styles.feasibility_notes: The generator does the 3D offline: rotate the vertex list for 40-60 frames and emit SMIL animate elements with a values list for each face's points (the researcher confirmed polygon-points animation in a Chromium ) or each edge's endpoints. Glenz: faces at fill-opacity 0.5 in two tints, optionally mix-blend-mode screen so overlaps brighten; no depth sorting needed. Wireframe: lines only, a few KB. Vector balls and dots: circles with animated cx, cy and r; SVG cannot re-sort by depth mid-loop, so keep dots identical and additive, or choose a motion where order never flips. Metaballs: circles moved by CSS keyframes inside a group filtered with feGaussianBlur then an feColorMatrix alpha threshold (the 'gooey' trick, tested by the researcher); the filter re-renders every frame, so keep its region small. CSS rotateY on SVG groups gives no usable perspective: do not rely on CSS 3D. An icosahedron glenz at 48 frames is about 20-40 KB.
styles.caveats: These effects are generic and free to use. Do not lift an object model that doubles as a group's mascot, or the surrounding logos. Removed as unverified: a jelly-cubes cracktro and a dots-on-sine-curves 10k intro that the submitted research cited without links, and the often-repeated claim that Second Reality is the PC reference for glenz (Wikipedia's article on it names no glenz). The red balls in Deviance's 2006 cracktro are called bouncing spheres by commenters, not glenz. Keep rotation slow; flickering translucent faces are unpleasant at header size, and the goo filter can stutter on phones.

styles.name: Texture movers: rotozoomer and tunnel
styles.era: Mid-90s chunky-pixel effects; in PC cracktros 1996-2007 (Hybrid with SAC, Halcyon for Paradigm on DOS; Paradox with Chemical Reaction, Razor, Genesis on Windows)
styles.what_it_is: Two effects that fill the frame by moving a texture rather than an object. The rotozoomer spins and scales a tiled image about the centre; the tunnel maps a texture onto the inside of an endless tube using precomputed distance and angle tables, so shifting the lookups makes you fly forward while the walls rotate. Both were standard ways to fill the space behind a logo, and commenters are blunt when they are done badly (Razor's 2001 rotozoomer is called slow and blocky, Paradox's 2000 tunnel 'disgusting' but charming).
visual_signature: Rotozoomer: one small tile repeated to infinity, rotating and breathing in and out so its grid lines sweep across the screen; a grey embossed tile under a pastel logo decorated with pixel fruit in Hybrid's Alien Incident cracktro
A metallic figure texture rotozoomed in a window beside the text block, with ornate metal bars top and bottom (Razor Blue Shift cracktro, 2001)

Tunnel with a perforated wall: a blue-grey tube punched with round holes, a row of glowing blue lights receding into it and a rough golden rock hanging in the centre (Halcyon for Paradigm, Rogue Squadron cracktro)

Nested-squares tunnel: about a dozen white-outlined squares, each rotated a little more than the last, shrinking to a dark centre on black, with lines of white text set at odd angles in perspective around it (Razor's ViRiLiTY 2000th cracktro, 2003)
Blurred feedback tunnel in murky green behind a teal bevelled logo and a dashed text block (Paradox/Chemical Reaction cracktro; commenters praise the feedback and dislike the blur)
Checker tunnel and '3D plasma tunnel' in a 4k: green/teal checker walls, then concentric red plasma rings (Genesis Cracktro #3, 2007)
Text sits on top in a plain block or on a solid panel; the effect is the background
styles.palette: Rotozoomers use two-tone tiles (grey on grey, metal). Tunnels are usually one cool hue darkening toward the centre (blue-grey, teal, murky green), stark white lines on black for the nested-squares kind, or red-orange rings for the plasma tunnel.
styles.typography: The host cracktro's bitmap font over the effect, with an outline or a solid text panel for legibility.
styles.motion: Rotozoomer: steady rotation with a slower zoom oscillation and a drifting centre. Tunnel: constant forward motion, slow roll, the vanishing point wandering on a sine path (mechanism per Lode Vandevenne's tutorial).

references.what: Hybrid and SAC, Alien Incident Cracktro (DOS; Demozoo: 7 Aug 1996; code Hetero, logo Dream Design, music Emax): logo plus rotozoom
Razor 1911 Half-Life Blue Shift cracktro (June 2001; code Parasight, graphics kemical, music zalza): 'slow and ugly rotozoomer with blocky movement'
Halcyon for Paradigm, Rogue Squadron cracktro (DOS; Pouet: Feb 1998; Demozoo: 29 Nov 1998; code Blitz, music Croaker): perforated tunnel with lights
ViRiLiTY 2000th Release Cracktro (Razor 1911, July 2003; music Dubmood): nested rotating squares
Paradox and Chemical Reaction cracktro (Pouet: May 2000; Demozoo: 2002; code neoman, logo alien^PDX): blurred feedback tunnel
Genesis Cracktro #3 with Neural (June 2007, a 4k by hitchhikr shown at SceneCON 2007): checkerboard effect and 3D plasma tunnel
Lode Vandevenne's tunnel tutorial: distance and angle lookup tables, animation by shifting texture coordinates

styles.readme_translation: Rotozoomer: an 800x160 band of rotating, zooming tiles made from the project's own monogram, with the wordmark on a solid strip above and text below. Tunnel: a full-width strip of nested squares or rings rushing outward with the project name on a solid plate in the centre. Either also works as the background layer of another style here.
styles.feasibility_notes: Rotozoomer is easy (researcher tested in Chromium): a <pattern> whose patternTransform carries two SMIL animateTransform elements, rotate plus scale with additive=sum, gives a true rotozoom in under 1 KB with any vector tile. Tunnel: a texture-mapped tunnel needs per-pixel lookups and is not possible, but the nested-shape tunnel is: 12-16 squares or rings, each scaling from 0 to beyond the frame on one shared keyframe with evenly staggered negative delays and an exponential timing curve, vector-effect non-scaling-stroke or stroke width keyed to scale, a small rotation offset per ring, and the group's centre on a slow sine path; a radial gradient overlay darkens the centre. Firefox and Safari behaviour of the animated patternTransform is unverified.
styles.caveats: Generic effects, free to use; do not reuse the textures or logos of the cited cracktros. Dates conflict between databases for two references (Rogue Squadron: Feb vs 29 Nov 1998; Paradox: May 2000 vs 2002). The genesis 4k's music is called a rip of an Amiga tune by commenters, unrelated to the visuals. These are the effects most likely to cause motion discomfort: keep rotation under about 45 degrees per second, confine them to a band, and freeze under prefers-reduced-motion.

left_out: 'Lit and liquid: bump-lit logo, mirror floor, metaballs' removed as a standalone style. It was a grab-bag of three effects from unrelated productions with one leg unconfirmed at submission. Mirror floor, environment-mapped solids and the lit-relief logo (now with one named example, the Paradox/Chemical Reaction cracktro) were merged into 'Win32 new old-school cracktro'; metaballs and the flat-blob variant were merged into 'Vector objects'. No reference was lost.
Fire effect sub-variant removed from the plasma style: no named PC cracktro confirmed, and true per-pixel fire is not achievable in a scriptless SVG anyway.

Not promoted to styles (agreeing with the researcher's own dead ends, after viewing the screenshots): the 1998-2000 Win9x painted-art Razor cracktros #15-#17 and #25 (they depend on a bitmap illustration, not reproducible as vector within the size limit and not reusable art); Razor's 2002 Soviet-poster parody cracktro (political-symbol and portrait-likeness risk); Razor's 2006 cartoon-in-a-TV and 2010 'tv noise' cracktros (too close to the existing phosphor-CRT style); Razor's 2007 keygen templates (the keygen-dialog style already exists, and the mascot is a credited artist's character).

Two styles were added rather than dropped, for Razor coverage: 'Text-mode poster installer (Razor 1911, 2024-26)', split out of the skinned-installer style because it can be delivered as pure text, and 'BIOS setup hijack' (Razor's CMOS Cosmos, 1st at Compusphere 2025), which the research missed.

families.title: C64, Amiga and Atari ST
families.overview:
Checked against the sources, the 8-bit and 16-bit side holds up as a family of machine-specific schools, and all eleven submitted styles survive with corrections. I added three that the research skipped and the owner or brief asked for: an Amiga-era Razor 1911 cracktro school (the Sector9 intros of 1990-91), bobs and dot objects, and the copper-only screen.

C64 (about 1986-92): black 320x200 screen, 16 fixed colours, 8x8 character cells, 24x21 sprites. Logos are character mosaics or expanded sprites, colour comes from raster splits by scanline, motion is per character (DYCP). The same cells give PETSCII pictures and disk-directory art, the one pure-text style here.

Amiga (about 1988-93): 32 colours from 4096, plus a copper that changes colour per scanline. It runs from megademo and trainer menus, through single-effect screens (vertical "Kefrens" bars, bob chains, copper-only colour fields), to the 1992 design break of Melon Dezign's flat colour and Spaceballs' silhouettes. The hand-pixelled chrome logo is a separate static tradition.

Atari ST (about 1988-91): 16 colours from 512, so it leans on per-scanline palette changes, very large gradient scroller fonts and digitised pictures, in UK compilation "menu disks" and in megademos with game-like menus.

On the owner's questions. Razor 1911: their Amiga years are in this family and are now a style; the better-known PC-era Razor look belongs to the PC family. Chiptune: within this family it can only be the silent track-list jukebox. Vaporwave and NFO ASCII artists are outside this family.

Most styles translate well to SVG because they are flat rectangles, stepped gradients and sine motion. Web search ran out part-way, so the "graffiti" pixel-logo school named in the brief could not be sourced and is left out instead of written from memory.

styles.name: C64 one-screen crack intro: raster-split logo and text on colour bars
styles.era: 1986-1989, Commodore 64 cracking scene (Europe, plus NTSC intros from the US such as Eagle Soft); small intros placed in front of cracked games
styles.what_it_is: The single-screen C64 intro: a group logo at the top, a few centred lines naming the game, cracker and date, and a scroller, all on black. Commenters on the C64 intro database call the Fairlight one "one of the most used intros ever" and the Eagle Soft one "THE C64-intro". It differs from the existing C64 boot/loader style: no BASIC screen and no loading stripes, only the intro itself.
visual_signature: Pure black screen and border, everything centred on a 40-column grid
Logo as one flat shape whose colour changes in horizontal bands by scanline: Dynamic Duo's two-row logo in red/green/yellow/blue bands; Ikari's upright slab capitals in blue and yellow bands
Logo drawn as an outline over a block of raster stripes: Fairlight's thin pink outlined letters sit on green/white stripes between two red rules
Logo as a mosaic of small bevelled squares: Triad's grey block-grid letters, about 6 character rows high, with one block blinking
Full-width raster bars about 8 pixels tall behind single text lines, shaded in 3-5 luminance steps (Fairlight: a pink bar behind the game title, a blue bar behind the 'CRACKED ... BY ...' line)
Fixed text block in 8x8 capitals: 'PRESENTS', game title, 'CRACKED ON dd/mm/yy BY handle', often fenced with dashes or dollar signs
One scroller near the bottom in double-width characters, plus optional 'PRESS SPACE'

Variants: brick-textured block letters on a blue panel above an orange brick wall panel with big yellow letters (Hotline); a multicolour bitmap picture panel in place of the logo with one grey label bar and a scroller under it (Eagle Soft)
styles.palette: The 16 fixed VIC-II colours on black. Pepto's measured values: black 000000, white FFFFFF, red 68372B, cyan 70A4B2, purple 6F3D86, green 588D43, blue 352879, yellow B8C76F, orange 6F4F25, brown 433900, light red 9A6759, dark grey 444444, grey 6C6C6C, light green 9AD284, light blue 6C5EB5, light grey 959595. Colours share luminance levels (blue = brown, red = dark grey, purple = orange, light blue = grey, green = light red, cyan = light grey, yellow = light green), so bar shading and fades run in ramps such as blue, light blue, cyan, white or brown, orange, yellow, white.
styles.typography: 8x8-pixel uppercase character sets, the ROM font or a redrawn one (thin 'computer' capitals, slab capitals). Logos are character mosaics or sprites doubled in X and Y, so edges step in 8-pixel or 2-pixel units. Scroller fonts are 1x1, 1x2 or 2x2 characters. Almost no lower case.
styles.motion: Raster colours roll vertically through the logo and the text bars; the scroller moves right to left at constant speed; one element may blink. Everything else is static. Motion is taken from user comments (colour rotation on Dynamic Duo, the logo blink on Triad); only stills were viewed.

references.what: Fairlight [FLT] 01 (code Woodo, packing Gollum; on-screen crack date 21.11.87): outlined logo on raster stripes, bars behind the text lines
Ikari 02 (code ExCell, music Laxity per comments; on-screen date 11/11/88): blue/yellow banded slab logo, orange and red text lines, blue two-line slogan
Triad 01 (on-screen date 87-20-DEC): grey block-grid logo, yellow tagline, one raster-washed info line; page notes say the logo colour coded the game's quality
Dynamic Duo [DD] 01 (1986, made by Flash of FCG/Radwar per the page): colour-banded logo, PRESS SPACE, wide scroller, no music
Hotline [HTL] 03 (1987, TMC per comments): brick-textured logo on a blue panel and an orange brick wall panel
Eagle Soft Incorporated [ESI] 02 (code Mitch, graphics Lady Hawk per comments): picture-panel variant
Cory Arcangel's 2002 interview with Linus Walleij of Triad: intros of 6-8 KB, 24x21 sprites expanded for blocky logotypes, fades ordered by luminosity, raster bars
Pepto's VIC-II palette analysis: colour names and luminance levels
Pepto's 2001 palette page: the hex values quoted above

styles.readme_translation: Above the fold: one animated SVG about 640x240 (2x scale of 320x120). Project name as the block logo with rolling raster bands, then PRESENTS, a one-line description on a raster bar, and a 'CRACKED ON' style line reused for version and date. The scroller carries the tagline or stats. Real links go in normal Markdown directly under the image.
